deck_title: 8-Way Model Routing Benchmark · OpenAI Decisions vs Microsoft Decision-1 (Switchyard v2.4.0 & v2.4.1)

cards.headline_prefix: OpenAI Decisions joins the 8-way routing test —
cards.subtitle: Across 960 decisions under cost-biased instructions (v2.4.0) and 2,760 decisions across 4 instruction variants (v2.4.1) on 40 bilingual prompts (20 EN / 20 ZH, 5 target models), Microsoft Decision-1 hits 37.7/40 (94.2%) -> 40/40 (100.0% neutral) at $7.6–$8.6/1M decisions, outperforming OpenAI Decisions (32/40 = 80.0% -> 37/40 = 92.5% neutral at $26.1–$28.4/1M).

workbench.title: Switchyard (satomic/model-router v2.4.0 & v2.4.1) · 8 Routing Approaches × 40 Bilingual Prompts
scenarios: Set A (20 explicit prompts: 10 EN + 10 ZH) & Set B (20 implicit/borderline prompts: 10 EN + 10 ZH)
5 candidate backends: gpt-4.1-mini (chat), gpt-4o (general), gpt-4.1 (coding), gpt-5.4 (reasoning), gpt-6-luna (creative)
Cloud System One APIs: TypeSafe Jev (jev-latest) & Microsoft Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry East US 2)
OpenAI Native API: POST /v1/decisions (locked to gpt-6-luna, $0.10/1M input, $0 output)
Local Open-Weight (M4 Pro 48GB): OpenJev 27B (MLX 4-bit, CC BY-NC 4.0) & Laya 0.3.20 (Apache-2.0)
General LLM Routers (/v1/chat/completions): gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-6-luna (reasoning=none), gpt-6-luna (default)
4 Instruction Variants (v2.4.1): neutral (default), cheap (v2.4.0 default), strong, bare
workbench.bands_note: Confidence gate (tau = 0.60): Act automatically if p >= 0.60 and instruction spread <= 2/40 (Jev, Decision-1); Confirm if p < 0.60 fallback or moderate instruction sensitivity (OpenAI Decisions, OpenJev, LLM mini/luna-none); Send to a human if high-confidence wrong picks or unstable CoT flips (luna-default, Laya).

decisions.question: Which cloud decision API delivers the best accuracy, calibration, and cost trade-off?
decisions.closest_label: 3.3x cheaper than OpenAI Decisions ($26.1–$28.4/1M) & 2.8x cheaper than Jev ($21.7–$24.1/1M)

decisions.question: Minimum accuracy across all 4 instruction styles (neutral / cheap / strong / bare)
decisions.closest_label: Removing 1 cost-bias sentence lifts Decision-1 +2.3, OpenJev +3.0, OpenAI +5.0 prompts

decisions.question: Does a p < 0.60 fallback gate cleanly intercept routing misses across all 480 calls?
decisions.selected_answer: Yes for Jev (3/3 caught) & Decision-1 (0 misses outside cheap); No for OpenAI (24/48 >= 0.60)
decisions.closest_label: OpenAI Decisions assigns up to p=0.78 on wrong picks to gpt-4.1-mini

callouts.lead: Removing the single cost-saving sentence ('Prefer a cheaper, faster model when the request is simple...') raises Jev, Decision-1, and OpenJev to 40/40 (100.0%).
callouts.body: OpenAI Decisions jumps from 32/40 (80.0%) to 37/40 (92.5%) under neutral instructions (and 38/40 = 95.0% under bare), confirming it is highly sensitive to cost-saving wording while still trailing Decision-1 in accuracy, calibration, and cost ($26.1 vs $7.6/1M).

callouts.lead: Across all 480 decisions in v2.4.1, 100% of OpenAI Decisions' 48 wrong picks routed the request to gpt-4.1-mini.
callouts.body: Specifically, 33/48 downgraded higher-tier tasks to gpt-4.1-mini and 15/48 routed creative writing (gpt-6-luna) sideways to gpt-4.1-mini. On B9 and B14, OpenAI Decisions never selected the right model under any of the 4 instructions.

cards.headline: 8 routing approaches across v2.4.0 (cost-biased) & v2.4.1 (neutral): full scorecard

rows.question: Microsoft Decision-1 (Foundry East US 2 · P50 541–597ms · P95 1.25–1.34s · $7.6–$8.6/1M)
OpenJev 27B (MLX 4-bit 15.6GB · P50 2,276–2,566ms · P95 2,597–3,030ms · $0 API · CC BY-NC 4.0)
Self-hosted Laya 0.3.20 (196MB · P50 111–127ms · P95 143–491ms · $0 API · Apache-2.0)
LLM: gpt-6-luna default reasoning (Foundry · P50 2,079–2,132ms · P95 3.05–3.54s · $62.4–$63.1/1M)

callouts.lead: 3 System One engines (TypeSafe Jev, Microsoft Decision-1, OpenJev 27B) hit 40/40 (100.0%) under v2.4.1 neutral instructions.
callouts.body: Decision-1 achieves the same 40/40 accuracy as Jev at 1/3 the cost ($7.6 vs $24.1/1M) because it bills only 1 completion token (~180 input + 1 output at $0.042/1M), whereas Jev bills ~82 internal reasoning tokens.

callouts.lead: 5 approaches marked (✕) still miss 3 to 21 prompts under neutral instructions — and CoT reasoning actively harms LLM routing.
callouts.body: Enabling default reasoning on gpt-6-luna drops accuracy from 90.8% (luna-none) to 72.5% (luna-default) and causes 11–13/40 prompts to flip across rounds. Meanwhile, gpt-4.1-mini is the only engine whose errors (4/40) all over-escalate to stronger models.

cards.headline: OpenAI /v1/decisions vs Microsoft & TypeSafe /v1/systemone wire protocol
cards.transition: ↓ Switchyard (satomic/model-router v2.4.0 / v2.4.1) protocol adapter + confidence threshold gate (tau = 0.60) ↓

callouts.lead: Switchyard v2.4.0 also fixed a silent fallback bug for OpenAI reasoning models (gpt-6-luna) on Chat Completions.
callouts.body: gpt-6-luna rejects Chat Completions calls that pass legacy max_tokens or temperature when reasoning is active (HTTP 400). Earlier router versions caught the exception and silently fell back to default gpt-4.1-mini (recording 0 ms); v2.4.0 uses max_completion_tokens and adds decision_reasoning_effort.

callouts.lead: Asymmetric instruction response: 'Prefer cheaper' hurts every dedicated engine (-2.5 to -12.5 pts), while 'Prefer stronger' never causes over-escalation.
callouts.body: Across all 480 calls per engine in v2.4.1, 100% of errors in Jev (3/3), Decision-1 (9/9), OpenJev (18/18), and OpenAI Decisions (48/48: 33 cheaper + 15 sideways to gpt-4.1-mini) erred toward cheaper models — zero errors ever picked a stronger model than needed.

cards.headline: Why Microsoft Decision-1 stays the #1 production choice after OpenAI Decisions joins
good_fit: Microsoft Decision-1 as default cloud router on Azure AI Foundry: 100% neutral accuracy (94.2% cheap), $7.6–$8.6/1M cost (3.3x cheaper than OpenAI Decisions, 16x cheaper than gpt-4.1-mini), ~550 ms P50, and clean 0.60 threshold gating
TypeSafe Jev when maximum instruction immunity (39..40/40 across all 4 variants, 0 false blocks at 0.60) and lowest cloud latency (~330 ms P50) justify ~3x Decision-1's price ($21.7–$24.1/1M)
Neutral routing instructions ('Pick the option whose description best matches...') while encoding tier boundaries inside candidate descriptions (+12.5% on OpenAI Decisions, +5.8% on Decision-1)
OpenAI Decisions for teams already on an OpenAI 1P key needing a fast (~400 ms P50) drop-in endpoint under neutral/bare instructions (92.5%–95.0%)
Setting reasoning_effort='none' whenever using a reasoning LLM (gpt-6-luna) as a prompt-based router (+15.0 to +18.3 pts accuracy, -400 ms latency, -37% cost vs default reasoning)
not_for: Combining OpenAI Decisions with cost-saving prompt instructions ('prefer cheaper when simple'): accuracy drops to 80.0% (32/40) and 14/20 (70%) on implicit Set B requests
Relying on a 0.60 confidence gate with OpenAI Decisions: 50% of its misses (24/48 across v2.4.1) have p >= 0.60 (up to 0.78), failing silently without triggering fallback
Calling /openai/v1/decisions on Azure AI Foundry (returns HTTP 404; Foundry serves Decision-1 at /providers/microsoft/v1/systemone instead)
Leaving default reasoning enabled on LLM routers (gpt-6-luna default drops to 72.5%–75.8% accuracy and flips choices across rounds on 11–13/40 prompts)
Commercial production use of OpenJev 27B weights (CC BY-NC 4.0 non-commercial license) or 5-way general model routing with Laya 0.3.20 (47.5%–52.5% accuracy)
